title: Course design in the age of AI
abstract: arXiv:2607.18735v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: I develop a model of learning-by-doing and course design, and use it to study the impacts of artificial intelligence (AI). A myopic student faces a sequence of tasks that he can work on or delegate to AI. Work requires costly effort but builds skill; delegation requires no effort but builds no skill. A teacher designs the task sequence ("course") to maximize the student's skill development, given his choices to work or delegate. Without AI, the teacher makes earlier tasks more effort-intensive and later tasks more skill-intensive. With AI, the teacher must redesign early tasks to induce effort, leading to less skill development. If AI complements effort, then improvements in AI quality make high-skill students learn faster but low-skill students learn slower.

translated_abstract: 我构建了一个关于“干中学”与课程设计的模型，并用它来研究人工智能（AI）的影响。一个短视的学生面临一系列任务，他可以自己完成这些任务，也可以将其委托给AI。自己完成任务需要付出有成本的努力，但能积累技能；委托给AI则无需努力，但也无法积累技能。教师在学生自主完成或委托AI的选择约束下，设计任务序列（即“课程”），以最大化学生的技能发展。在没有AI的情况下，教师会让早期任务更偏重努力投入，后期任务更偏重技能运用。在有AI的情况下，教师必须重新设计早期任务以激励学生付出努力，从而导致技能发展的减少。如果AI与努力互补，那么AI质量的提升会使高技能学生学习得更快，但低技能学生学习得更慢。
tldr: 本文构建了“干中学”与课程设计模型，揭示AI的引入迫使教师重新设计早期任务以激励学生努力，从而减少技能积累，且AI质量提升会加快高技能学生的学习却拖慢低技能学生的学习。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a model of learning-by-doing and course design, showing that AI forces teachers to redesign early tasks to induce student effort—reducing skill development—and that improvements in AI quality accelerate learning for high-skill students but slow it for low-skill students.
